title: Backtested the 5 minute opening range breakout on NQ, 2021 to 2026. 1,281 trades, and the long side lost $48k in a bull market.
author: person-person12
selftext:
The opening range breakout is on every feed, so I ran the plainest version of it that can actually be written as rules, on NQ 5 minute candles from Nov 2021 to Oct 2026. Mark the high and low of the 09:30 candle, take the close that breaks either side, stop 1 ATR, target 2 ATR, one contract, no new entries after 15:30, commission and a quarter point of slippage on every fill. I ran it in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) over 353,153 real NQ candles.

**NQ 5m, Nov 2021 to Oct 2026, $100k account, 1 contract:**

* 1,281 trades
* 33.3% win rate
* payoff 1.81 to 1, $986 average win against $544 average loss
* profit factor 0.906
* net **-$43,905**
* max drawdown 48.5%
* worst losing streak 17 trades

The 33% win rate with a 1.8 payoff is the pair people say to aim for, lose small and win big and stop caring about hit rate. At 1.81 to 1 the break even hit rate is 35.6%, so it comes up two and a half points short and that gap is the whole result.

The side split is the part I didnt expect. **The long side lost $48,827 and the short side made $4,923**, over a window where NQ itself went up about 80%. Buying the break above the opening range through a five year bull market was the losing half of this.

Costs are $19,215 of the damage, $6,405 commission and $12,810 slippage across 1,281 round trips. Take every cost out and its still down about $24,700, so this isnt a fees story.

What gets taught publicly is the shape of it, not a rulebook. Theres no published stop, no published target, no cutoff time, and plenty of ppl use the first 15 or 30 minutes as the range instead of the first 5. I picked 1 ATR and 2 ATR because those are the defaults nobody argues with, and the 09:30 candle because its the strictest reading of it. A 30 minute range with a time stop is a different strategy and I havent run it.

The other thing I left out is the filter most ORB traders say they apply, which is only taking the break in the direction of the higher timeframe trend. Given where the long side landed, thats the next one I run.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: The long side losing money while NQ went up about 80% is the part I'd dig into. Feels like the long breakouts mostly bought the first push and got stopped on the pullback. Curious if the 15-30 min range changes that, or if it's mostly the costs.
